diagnosis: The left and centre panels show roughly 1000 pairs tied at the maximum within $10^{-15}$ and an average of about 13 contacts per point, comparable to the $162\times7-28=1106$ rotationally-reduced degrees of freedom, so the code is an isostatically jammed LP vertex polished to machine precision. That contact network is nevertheless highly unbalanced: contact counts range from about 2 to 27, many points have only 8--9 contacts, and one rattler has none, meaning the maximum is carried by a subset while at least one point contributes no constraint. Consequently the LP has essentially no feasible first-order descent direction, while the 33 programs all start from the same configuration and use either kicks small enough to fall back into the same basin or kicks large enough that short re-annealing cannot recover an equally good structure. The missing structural property is therefore not a better polish of this contact graph, but a different, more evenly stressed topology in which every point is active and positive contact stresses can equilibrate at every point.

The plot shows roughly $1000$ pairs tied within about $10^{-15}$ of the maximum—around $13$ contacts per point versus only $7$ tangent degrees of freedom per point—so the contact Jacobian is heavily overconstrained and no first-order descent direction remains. Small perturbations therefore snap back under LP polishing, while large perturbations merely produce worse amorphous optima; genuine progress requires changing the contact topology or construction class, with crash-proof fallbacks to the incumbent.

diagnosis: After 65 evaluations the gain is only $1.34\times10^{-6}$ because the incumbent is numerically jammed: the left panel shows at least 1,000 pairs with slack below $10^{-15}$, essentially saturating the $162\cdot7-28=1{,}106$ degrees of freedom. The contact graph is amorphous and inequitable—most points carry 8–26 contacts while one rattler carries none—so roughly one point is wasted while the other 161 are over-constrained. Any small Gaussian, hole-relocation, or LogSumExp perturbation is therefore pulled back by the trust-region LP, whose linearized feasible cone has no useful descent direction at machine-precision ties. The missing structural property is a balanced, parsimonious topology, ideally with algebraic/orbit regularity, in which contact load is shared equitably and no point is redundant, rather than an accidental near-isostatic jam with inequitable load.
